newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Elec building new TFT-LCD plant.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Elec building new TFT-LCD plant.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai Electronics Industries Co said on Thursday it had recently started building a factory to make thin-film transistor liquid crystal display (TFT-LCD) panels.
A Hyundai statement said it would invest 500 billion won in the plant, which would be capable of processing 600mm X 720mm mother glass sheets to make 13.3-inch or larger LCD panels.
It said the plant, capable of processing 360,000 sheets of mother glass per year to make 2.16 million panels of 13.3-inch LCDs, was due to begin full operation in August next year.
The factory's annual capacity was scheduled to double by the end of 1999 with an additional investment of 730 billion won, a company spokesman said.
Part of the additional investment would be used to build research and development facilities, he said.
He said Hyundai's existing factory had been operating since October last year and was capable of processing 144,000 sheets of 550mm X 650mm mother glass.
The factory was built with investment of 330 billion won, he said.
Once the planned investment was concluded in 1999, Hyundai's total production capacity would reach 4.8 million panels of 13.3-inch LCDs, the spokesman said.
The company is a unit of South Korea's largest Hyundai Group chips, telecommunications equipment, personal computers and automotive electronics devices.
Hyundai Electronics had targeted annual sales of about 4.1 trillion won this year from last year's 3.17 trillion won, the spokesman said.
LCD panels are mainly used in notebook computers but analysts say the panels are expected to replace many personal computer monitors in the future.
The Hyundai Electronics statement forecast the world market for TFT-LCD panels would increase to $10 billion this year from last year's $6.5 billion.
